<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VI.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|235}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=6|verse=50}}† This is the bread that descendeth from heauen: that if any man eate of it, he die not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=51}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel in a daily Masse for the dead.}}∷ I am the liuing bread, that came dovvne from heauen. If any man eate of this bread, he shal liue for euer: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 26. Mr. 14, 22. Lu. 22, 19. 1. Cor. 11, 24.''}}* the bread vvhich I vvil giue, is my flesh for the life of the vvorld.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=52}}† The Ievves therfore stroue among them selues, saying, {{sup|‖}} Hovv can this man giue vs his flesh to eate? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=53}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore said to them, Amen, amen I say to you, {{sup|‖}} Vnles you eate the flesh of the Sonne of man, {{sup|‖}} and drinke his bloud, {{sup|‖}} you shal not haue life in you. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=54}}† He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my bloud, hath life euerlasting: and {{sup|‖}} I vvil raise him vp in the last day.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=55}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō CORPVS CHRISTI day.}}For my flesh, is {{sup|‖}} meate in deede: and my bloud is drinke in deede. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=56}}† He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my bloud, abideth in me, and I in him. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=57}}† As the liuing father hath sent me, and I liue by the father: and he that eateth me, the same also shal liue by me. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=58}}† This is the bread that came dovvne from heauen. Not as your fathers did eate Manna, and died. {{sup|‖}} He that eateth this bread, shal liue for euer.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=59}}† These things he said teaching in the Synagogue, in Capharnáum.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=60}}† Many therfore of his Disciples hearing it, said, This saying is hard, and vvho can heare it? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=61}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving vvith him self that his Disciples murmured at this, he said to them, Doth this scandalize you? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=62}}† {{sup|‖}} If then you shal see {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 3, 13.''}}* the Sonne of man ascend vvhere he vvas before? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=63}}† It is the spirit that quickeneth, {{sup|‖}} the flesh profiteth nothing. The wordes that I haue spoken to you, be spirit and life. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=64}}† But there be certaine of you {{sup|‖}} that beleeue not. For {{sc|Iesvs}} knevv from the beginning vvho they vvere that did not beleeue, and vvho he vvas that vvould betray him. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=65}}† And he said, Therfore did I say to you, that no man can come to me, vnles it be giuen him of my Father. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=66}}† After this many of his Disciples {{sup|‖}} vvent backe: and novv they vvalked not vvith him.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=67}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore said to the Tvvelue, VVhat, vvil you also depart? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=68}}† Simon {{sup|‖}} Peter therfore ansvvered him, Lord, to vvhom shal vve goe? thou hast the vvordes of eternal life. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=69}}† And we beleeue and haue knovven that thou art Christ the sonne of God. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=70}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered them, Haue not I chosen you the Tvvelue: & of you one is a deuil? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=71}}† And he meant Iudas Iscariot, Simons sonne: for this same vvas to betray him, vvhereas he vvas one of the Tvvelue.<noinclude>{{rh||Gg ij|ANNOT.}}</noinclude>
